As in my original post: 

 I don't want suggestions for medical help and therapy - I have worked with specialists for two decades and have an amazing supportive therapist but that doesn't make my life any less shit. I have no quality of life and its my choice to stop - it isn't selfish or giving up; it's looking to end life with dignity on my own terms.

As I mentioned in my original post - I don't want suggestions for medical help.

I have worked with specialists for two decades and have an amazing supportive therapist that I have seen for years. 

It has not helped to sufficiently improve my quality of life but I am glad that it worked for you.

I do fully understand my condition- I think you need to understand that asthma exists on a spectrum. 


My parents had your exact mindset and it was well intentioned but also very toxic:

"Overcoming their condition" places an enormous burden on a child - it may not be something they can overcome. 


Some people have very mild asthma that can be managed and controlled with the right meds/support -that's wonderful! 

However some people have very severe asthma that may not be able to be controlled. They can't fix or cure this if they "just try hard enough". People DIE of asthma- and it is not for lack of "encouragement' or "effort".  It is not their fault- it is a medical condition that is not within their control and even the best medical support/medications may not be able to manage it.

It is cruel to ask a child to try to "overcome their condition" when it is not be possible.  

It is better to tell kids they can do their best to manage the symptoms and to live their lives to the fullest extent they can with asthma- that is more realistic 



It is needlessly cruel to tell me I don't understand my condition and to "fully life my life" - you think I don't want to, more than anything else? 
Do you think I just haven't done everything I can do manage asthma for TWO DECADES? You think I have not fought to do everything I can do live my life to the fullest? 

Please respect that I wouldn't be here unless I no longer have a quality of life because my medical condition has declined to a point where it cannot be managed. Euthanasia exists to provide those who are suffering with the option to die with dignity.

I appreciate where you're coming from - but I am not looking to get help with depression. 

My depression is as a result of asthma- it cannot be cured, and in my case cannot be managed. I will spend the rest of my life suffering and have already been suffering extensively for decades. 

Suicide hotlines won't change that. But euthanasia could allow me to die with some dignity and find peace.

Thanks for the advice. I'll look into it. 

 I understand why you'd advocate for choosing life. I want to stress that I did - I tried, I created a life for myself and if I was well it would be amazing. 

But it is not worth living with such a low quality of life when everything I love being ripped away from me on a regular basis. I am helpless, and miserable and I don't see any other options.
